item.title: AMEC Targets 60% High-End Market Coverage Within Five Years as China’s Chip Equipment Ambitions Grow
item.description:
Please note that this article cites information from The Paper , Mydrivers , and 21jingji .

China’s semiconductor equipment ambitions continue to expand. According to The Paper , AMEC Chairman Gerald Yin recently said the company aims to cover at least 60% of the high-end semiconductor equipment market over the next five years, making it the world’s most comprehensive semiconductor equipment supplier.

To achieve that goal, AMEC plans to expand its portfolio to more than 100 types of high-end semiconductor equipment, including most plasma etching tools, thin-film deposition equipment, as well as processing tools. The company also aims to become a first-tier global semiconductor equipment company by 2035 in terms of scale, product competitiveness, and customer satisfaction.

Yin said AMEC has deployed more than 8,800 process chambers across production lines at over 170 customers worldwide. The company’s cumulative installed base has grown by more than 35% annually over the past 14 years. Revenue per employee has reached RMB 4.55 million (approximately US$650,000), he added.

Meanwhile, AMEC continues to maintain a high level of R&D investment. According to The Paper, the company spent RMB 3.74 billion on research and development last year, accounting for 30.2% of revenue, above the average R&D intensity of companies listed on Shanghai’s STAR Market.

The company has also been expanding its manufacturing footprint. As the report indicates, AMEC has established R&D and production bases in five locations across China with a combined floor area of 600,000 square meters this year. The company plans to expand that to 900,000 square meters within the next five years, with a planned annual production capacity valued at no less than RMB 70 billion.

Etching Portfolio Drives Growth and Market Expansion

As Mydrivers points out, AMEC’s ambitious growth targets are underpinned by its etching equipment portfolio. By the end of 2025, the company had shipped more than 6,800 process chambers worldwide, with its global market share continuing to rise steadily. AMEC’s portfolio includes two major categories of plasma etching systems—capacitively coupled plasma (CCP) and inductively coupled plasma (ICP)—covering more than 20 product segments. The systems have been widely adopted by leading domestic and international customers, supporting etching applications from 65nm to 3nm.

Mydrivers adds that AMEC’s latest annual report showed record financial results for 2025. Revenue reached RMB 12.385 billion, up 36.62% year over year, while net profit attributable to shareholders rose by RMB 496 million, or 30.69%, to approximately RMB 2.111 billion.

Meanwhile, on July 27, CXMT debuted on Shanghai’s STAR Market. According to 21jingji , the listing also quickly created ripple effects across the semiconductor equipment supply chain. The report notes that key equipment suppliers include Hwatsing Technology, AMEC, and Piotech. Notably, AMEC disclosed that its capacitively coupled plasma (CCP) etching systems have entered volume production across multiple key DRAM process steps at CXMT, while its next-generation high-aspect-ratio etching systems are currently undergoing production-line qualification.

item.title: NAND’s 2026 Playbook: Samsung, SK hynix Chase Upgrades and SSD Mix Over Volume
item.description:
Please note that this article cites information from Newspim , DataNews , News Tomato , The Bell , ETNews and SK hynix .

Ahead of Kioxia’s earnings call today, Samsung and SK hynix’s 2Q26 results, released earlier this week, both point to NAND Flash’s return as a key growth driver. Crucially, ASP gains, rather than shipment growth, are driving the recovery. With major capacity expansion not expected until 2028–29, memory makers appear to be prioritizing supply discipline and process/product upgrades to support pricing power instead of aggressively chasing demand growth.

The trend is evident in both companies’ NAND results. According to SK hynix , NAND bit shipments grew around 15% QoQ in 2Q26, while ASPs surged by the mid-50% range. Samsung saw an even stronger pricing impact, with NAND shipments rising only low-single digits QoQ while ASPs jumped by the high-60% range, Newspim reports.

SK hynix Expands NAND Migration Across Korea and China

According to DataNews , SK hynix’s NAND revenue is estimated to have soared 358.7% YoY to KRW 21.4161 trillion in 2Q26, while operating profit more than doubled QoQ to KRW 13.52 trillion from KRW 5.67 trillion, based on brokerage estimates.

Despite the sharp earnings rebound, SK hynix remains cautious on NAND bit demand, projecting third-quarter bit shipments to rise only in the low-single digits QoQ. For full-year 2026, the company expects NAND demand growth to remain in the high-teens YoY range.

The outlook suggests the recovery is being driven less by volume than by stronger pricing and technology upgrades. To reinforce profitability, SK hynix is accelerating process migration, with 321-layer NAND now accounting for the largest share of its output. The company aims to expand the node to 50% of its domestic NAND production capacity by the end of 2026.

The strategy extends beyond Korea. According to News Tomato , SK hynix has completed the transition to 192-layer NAND and replaced legacy equipment at its first Dalian fab in China. Meanwhile, The Bell reports the company has begun preparations for mass production of mid-200-layer Floating Gate (FG) NAND at Dalian Fab 2, with a pilot “One Path” line scheduled for the third quarter to validate process stability and yields.

Beyond process migration, product mix optimization is also supporting SK hynix’s NAND profitability. SSDs are taking a larger share of NAND revenue, rising from around 50% in 2Q25 to the 60% range in 1Q26 and roughly 70% in 2Q26, DataNews adds.

Samsung Shifts NAND Strategy Toward AI SSDs and Next-Gen V-NAND

Similarly, Samsung Electronics is shifting its NAND strategy toward AI-driven enterprise SSDs. According to ETNews , fueled by surging demand for dedicated KV cache storage amid the rise of agentic AI, the company expects eSSDs to account for more than 60% of NAND revenue in 2026, up over 20 percentage points YoY.

Meanwhile, Samsung is advancing both performance and capacity upgrades across its SSD portfolio. ETNews reports that it aims to target early AI platform adoption with ultra-high-speed PCIe Gen6 SSDs, while expanding shipments of 256TB high-capacity eSSDs based on V9 1Tb QLC NAND. The company’s QLC-based SSD shipments are expected to more than double in 2H26 compared with 1H26, the report adds.

Notably, Samsung is also preparing its next-generation NAND technology. The company plans to begin mass production of V10 NAND in August, introducing new bonding technology and a three-step process for the first time, according to ETNews.

This shift toward process migration and product optimization reflects a broader industry strategy. According to TrendForce , NAND suppliers are boosting bit output primarily through technology migration rather than major capacity expansion in 2026. However, supply growth is expected to accelerate in 2027 as higher-layer NAND migration and new fabs ramp up, potentially pushing the market toward oversupply in 2H27 amid weak consumer demand and renewed pricing pressure, TrendForce notes.

item.title: DDR5 MRDIMMs Gain Momentum; Renesas Unveils 16,000 MT/s Chipset as AMD Reportedly Eyes Adoption
item.description:
Please note that this article cites information from Wccftech , Renesas, ZDNet , JEDEC , Weekly Post , Economic Daily,  News , Innodisk , and ITHome .

DDR5 MRDIMMs are gaining traction as rising compute demand drives memory makers to accelerate their product roadmaps. According to Wccftech , Renesas has unveiled a new MRDIMM chipset solution capable of enabling DDR5 MRDIMM speeds of up to 16,000 MT/s, up to 25% faster than the previous generation. The company adds that it has also begun sampling its latest MRDIMM MRCD (RRG5013x) and MDB devices to select customers, including all major DRAM suppliers, with production availability expected in the second half of 2027.

Among Renesas’ partners, AMD may be one of the key adopters of the company’s latest MRDIMM solution, as Wccftech indicates. The report notes that the company has already outlined DDR5-12800 MRDIMM support for its Zen 6 Venice and Verano platforms, and its future Florence “Zen 7” processors could support even faster MRDIMMs.

MRDIMM is a next-generation DDR5 server memory technology designed for AI and high-performance computing (HPC) workloads. By enabling simultaneous operation of two memory ranks, it significantly increases memory bandwidth while remaining compatible with existing DDR5 platforms, according to ZDNet , citing JEDEC .

The industry views MRDIMM as a key memory technology that will drive the server market before DDR6 reaches widespread adoption rather than as a replacement for DDR6, Weekly Post notes. Its ability to deliver DDR6-class bandwidth while remaining compatible with existing platforms is expected to accelerate adoption.

Commercial products are also beginning to emerge. According to Economic Daily News , Innodisk unveiled its DDR5-12800 MRDIMM memory modules, offering up to 60% higher bandwidth than DDR5-8000 RDIMMs while maintaining compatibility with existing DDR5 RDIMM slots.

The JEDEC roadmap outlines the next phase of MRDIMM development. According to ITHome , citing the JEDEC roadmap, the second-generation MRDIMM standard is nearing completion with support for speeds of up to 12,800 MT/s, while third-generation MRDIMMs are expected to reach up to 17,600 MT/s around 2030.

MRDIMMs Gain Momentum Across the AI Server Ecosystem

Major memory vendors are also expanding their MRDIMM portfolios. According to Wccftech, Micron has introduced MRDIMMs with speeds of up to 14,400 MT/s for AI server applications. On the platform side, Intel is among the first to support 8,800 MT/s MRDIMMs on its Xeon 6 processors, while AMD is targeting support for speeds of up to 12,800 MT/s.
